Date: Friday, June 19, 2026

Selected Approach:
- Correct the field + normalize the value for display

Approved implementation approach:
Change line 232 to read accountSubtype (lowercase t) so the real subtype flows through, and title-case the value for display ("savings" → "Savings") so it's consistent with the existing 'Checking' fallback. One method (formatAccountDisplay()), frontend-only, no logic change anywhere else.

Andrew's Answers:
Q: Display casing. The backend stores the Plaid subtype lowercase (e.g. "savings"). Should I title-case it for display ("Savings", consistent with the existing "Checking" fallback) — or render it exactly as Plaid returns it? My recommendation: title-case it for a clean, consistent line. Optional
  A (Andrew confirmed your prediction): Title-case it — show 'Savings' / 'Checking' so it's consistent with the fallback; don't ship a lowercase 'savings'.
Q: Null-subtype fallback. When Plaid genuinely returns no subtype, the current code defaults to 'Checking' — which is the very assumption that caused this bug. Keep 'Checking', or use a neutral label like 'Account' so we never assert a type we don't actually know? My recommendation: neutral "Account" for the unknown case. Optional
  A (Andrew confirmed your prediction): Use a neutral 'Account' when the subtype is unknown — don't keep falsely defaulting to 'Checking'.

Proceed with implementation.
